sections.text:
sync: tolerate over-delivery on max_count=1 ancestor probes
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/11

## Why

\`Node::check_shared_block_via_events\` (IBD path, \`src/network/sync.rs:4658\`) and \`run_tip_forward_validation\`'s path-2a ancestor probe (tip-validation path, \`src/network/sync.rs:7708\`) both reject any \`GetHeaders\` response with \`headers.len() > 1\`. The probe only ever consumes \`hdrs[0]\`, so the rejection only guards against an upper-bound-abuse vector that the server side already caps at \`MAX_GETBLOCKS_ITEMS = 64\` (≈12 KB per response, dwarfed by the Argon2 verification that the probe gates).

It bricks any pre-v1.9.2 peer in the network. Those peers ignored \`max_count\` and returned up to 64 headers in a single response. Observed live on \`exfer-node-stack\` (fly.io, performance-1x, v1.11.0):

\`\`\`
07:07:45 INFO  New tip: height=605656 …                       ← last block accepted
07:09:45 WARN  Sync manager: Stage B run_ibd failed via [223,97,230,230]: IBD block timeout
07:16:34 WARN  Sync manager: IBD failed: ancestor probe at height 605656 returned 64 headers, expected 1
07:17:38 WARN  Sync manager: IBD failed: ancestor probe at height 605656 returned 64 headers, expected 1
07:18:43 WARN  Sync manager: IBD failed: ancestor probe at height 605656 returned 64 headers, expected 1
07:19:48 WARN  Sync manager: IBD failed: ancestor probe at height 605656 returned 64 headers, expected 1
07:20:53 WARN  Sync manager: IBD failed: IBD peer disconnected  ← 5th strike, peer dropped
[+16 h]                                                          ← no further "starting IBD" log line
\`\`\`

The dropped peer was the only one with \`ever_confirmed_for_ibd=true\` (set during Stage B anchor-apply at h=500,000 earlier in the same boot). After it dropped, \`should_ibd\` returned \`None\` on every subsequent poll because the remaining 7 peers' background tip validation kept timing out (\`deadline exceeded\`), none could reach \`tip.confirmed=true\`, and none had the sticky flag. Mainnet advanced from 619,068 → 626,186 over the same 16 hours while the local tip stayed pinned at 605,656.

## What

Drop the \`headers.len() != 1\` rejection at both sites. Validate only \`hdrs[0].height == requested_height\` (a real protocol violation, since \`hdrs[0]\` is the single header consumed by the probe). Extras are informational and discarded.

The post-receive logic is extracted into a pure free function:

\`\`\`rust
fn interpret_ancestor_probe_response(
    headers: &[BlockHeader],
    expected_height: u64,
    our_block_id_at_height: Option<Hash256>,
) -> Result<Option<bool>, String>
\`\`\`

so the I/O-free part is unit-testable. \`check_shared_block_via_events\` now delegates to this helper; the path-2a probe inlines the same shape (it has an existing per-call type structure that wouldn't gain from the helper).

## What doesn't change

* Server-side \`GetHeaders\` handler still clamps \`req.max_count\` to \`MAX_GETBLOCKS_ITEMS = 64\` (\`sync.rs:4172\`). Over-delivery is bounded by the same cap that already protects every other GetHeaders consum
